page: Google Cloud Platform n4d-highcpu-2 is a compute-optimized virtual machine featuring 2 vCPUs and 4 GB of RAM, yielding a 2.0 GB memory-per-core ratio. Powered by an AMD EPYC 9B45 processor utilizing the x86_64 architecture, this instance allocates 1 physical core with 2 threads per core on a dedicated basis. The CPU cache configuration includes 48 KB of L1d cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache. It does not include local storage or bundled GPUs, and provides zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark results highlight strong single-core capabilities alongside constrained multi-core and memory performance. The instance achieves top-tier status in single-core metrics, including a stress-ng single-core score of 3437.06, a Geekbench single-core score of 2493.0, and high single-threaded compression throughput with 37.39 GB/sec in gzip and 16.63 GB/sec in bzip3. Conversely, multi-core and memory-intensive benchmarks fall into the bottom 25%, as evidenced by a multi-core Geekbench score of 3185.0 and a Passmark memory score of 1516.31. Large-block uncached memory read and write speeds remain average at 45.68 GB/sec and 26.65 GB/sec, respectively.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the n4d-highcpu-2 offers a dense, dedicated compute profile suitable for workloads that prioritize single-threaded execution over massive parallel processing or large memory footprints. Given the lack of local storage and the 4 GB RAM limitation, it is not designed for memory-heavy databases or complex multi-threaded compilations. Instead, it is best suited for lightweight single-threaded tasks, basic text processing, static web serving, and low-intensity utility workloads.
